51. Empower Developers

作者：Timothy High

Things are usually easier said than done, and software architects are notoriously good at coming up with things to say. To keep your words from becoming a lot of hot air (generally the key ingredient in making vaporware), you need a good team of developers. The role of an architect is usually to impose constraints, but you also have the opportunity to be an enabler. To the extent your responsibilities allow, you should do everything possible to empower your developers.

事情通常说起来容易做起来难，而软件架构师出了名地擅长出主意。为了不让你的话变成一堆热空气（那通常是 vaporware 的关键成分），你需要一个好的开发团队。架构师的角色通常是施加约束，但你也有机会做赋能者。在你职责允许的范围内，你应该尽一切可能赋能你的开发。

Make sure developers have the tools they need. Tools shouldn’t be imposed on developers, they should be carefully chosen to make sure they are the right tools for the job at hand. Repetitive and mindless work should be automated wherever possible. Also, it is well worth the investment to make sure developers have top-notch machines to work with, adequate network bandwidth, and access to software, data, and information necessary to carry out their work.

确保开发有他们需要的工具。工具不该强加给开发，应该精心选择确保是手头工作的对的工具。重复无脑的工作应尽可能自动化。此外，确保开发有顶级机器、足够网络带宽、以及开展工作所需软件、数据和信息的访问权，非常值得投资。

Make sure they have the skills they need. If training is required, make sure they get it. Invest in books and promote active discussions about technology. The work life of a developer should be hands-on and practical, but also should be actively academic. If you have the budget for it, send your team to technical presentations and conferences. If not, get them involved in technical mailing lists and look for free events in your city. As much as possible, participate in the developer selection process as well. Look for developers that are hungry

确保他们有需要的技能。如果需要培训，确保他们得到。投资书籍并推动关于技术的积极讨论。开发的工作生活应该动手实践，但也应该积极学术。如果预算允许，送团队去技术演讲和会议。如果没有，让他们参与技术邮件列表，找城市里的免费活动。也尽可能参与开发选拔过程。找渴望

to learn, that have that little “spark” that says they really dig technology (also make sure they can play ball with the team…). It’s hard to get a big bang out of a team of duds.

学习的开发，找那种真的热爱技术的小火花（也要确保他们能和团队合拍……）。一队庸才搞不出大动静。

Let developers make their own decisions wherever it won’t contradict the overall goal of the software design. But put constraints where they count, not only to guarantee quality, but also to further empower developers. Create standards for the sake of consistency, but also to reduce the number of troublesome, insignificant decisions that aren’t part of the essential problem developers are solving. Create a clear roadmap for where to put their source files, what to call them, when to create new ones, and so on. This will save them time.

在不与软件设计整体目标矛盾的地方，让开发自己做决定。但在关键处施加约束，不仅为保证质量，也为进一步赋能开发。为一致性创建标准，但也为了减少那些不属于开发要解决的本质问题的麻烦、无足轻重的决定。为源文件放哪、叫什么、什么时候建新的等创建清晰路线图。这会省他们时间。

Lastly, protect developers from nonessential parts of their job. Too much paperwork and too many office chores add overhead and reduce their effectiveness. You (usually) aren’t a manager, but you can have influence on the processes surrounding software development. Whatever processes are used, make sure they are designed to remove obstacles, not increase them.

最后，保护开发不受工作中非必要部分的干扰。太多文书和办公室杂事增加开销、降低效率。你（通常）不是经理，但你可以影响围绕软件开发的流程。不管用什么流程，确保它们是为消除障碍而设计的，而不是增加障碍。

Timothy High Timothy High is a software architect with more than 15 years’ experience with web, multitiered client-server, and application-integration technologies. He is currently working as a software architect for Sakonnet Technologies, a leader in Energy Trading and Risk Management (ETRM) software.

Timothy High Timothy High 是有 15 年以上 Web、多层客户端-服务器和应用集成技术经验的软件架构师。他目前是 Sakonnet Technologies（能源交易与风险管理 ETRM 软件领导者）的软件架构师。

52. Record Your Rationale

作者：Timothy High

There is much debate in the software development community about the value of documentation, especially with regard to the design of the software itself. The disagreements generally cluster around the perceived value of doing a “big upfront design,” and the difficulties of maintaining design documentation synchronized with an ever-changing code base.

软件开发社区里关于文档价值有很多争论，特别是关于软件本身的设计。分歧通常集中在做「大前期设计」的感知价值，以及保持设计文档和不断变化的代码库同步的困难上。

One type of documentation that ages well, doesn’t require much effort, and almost always pays off is a record of the rationale behind decisions that are made regarding the software architecture. As explained in Mark Richards’s axiom “Architectural Tradeoffs,” the definition of a software architecture is all about choosing the right tradeoffs between various quality attributes, cost, time, and other factors. It should be made clear to you, your managers, developers, and other software stakeholders why one solution was chosen over another and what tradeoffs this entailed. (Did you sacrifice horizontal scalability in the name of reducing hardware and licensing costs? Was security such a concern that it was acceptable to increase the overall response time in exchange for data encryption?)

一类不会过时、不需要太多努力、几乎总有回报的文档，是关于软件架构决策背后理由的记录。正如 Mark Richards 公理「架构权衡」所说，软件架构的定义就是在各种质量属性、成本、时间和其他因素之间选对权衡。应该向你、你的经理、开发和其他软件干系人说清楚：为什么选一个方案而不是另一个，这带来了什么权衡。（你是为了降低硬件和许可成本牺牲了水平扩展吗？安全是不是重要到可以接受增加整体响应时间来换取数据加密？）

The exact format of this documentation can vary according to what is appropriate for your project, from quick notes in a text document, wiki, or blog, to using a more formal template to record all aspects of each architectural decision. Whatever the form and format, the documentation should answer the basic questions “What was that decision we made?”, and “Why did we make that decision?”. A secondary question that is often asked and should be documented is “What other solutions were considered, and why were they rejected?” (actually, the question usually asked is, “Why can’t we do it my way?”). The documentation should also be searchable so that you can easily find it whenever it’s needed.

这个文档的确切格式可以根据项目合适程度变化，从文本文档、wiki 或博客里的快速笔记，到用更正式模板记录每个架构决策的各方面。不管形式格式如何，文档应该回答基本问题：「我们做了什么决定？」以及「为什么做这个决定？」。一个常被问到、也该记录的次要问题是：「考虑了什么其他方案，为什么被拒？」（实际上，常被问的是：「为什么不能按我的方式做？」）文档还应该可搜索，以便需要时容易找到。

This documentation may come in handy in a number of situations:

这个文档在很多情况下会派上用场：

As a means of communication to developers regarding important archi- • tectural principles that should be followed

作为向开发传达应遵循的重要架构原则的沟通手段

To get the team “on the same page,” or even head off a mutiny, when devel- • opers question the logic behind the architecture (or even to humbly accept criticism if it turns out a decision doesn’t hold up under scrutiny)

让团队「达成共识」、甚至在开发质疑架构背后逻辑时避免哗变（或者如果某个决定经不起审视，也谦卑地接受批评）

To show managers and stakeholders exactly why the software is being • built the way it is (such as why an expensive piece of hardware or software is necessary)

向经理和干系人准确展示软件为什么这么建（比如为什么需要昂贵的硬件或软件）

When handing off the project to a new architect (how many times have • you inherited a piece of software and wondered exactly why the designers did it THAT way?)

把项目交给新架构师时（你多少次接手一个软件、纳闷设计者为什么那么做？）

However, the most important benefits that come from this practice are:

然而，这个实践带来的最重要好处是：

It forces you to be explicit about your reasoning in order to verify that • your foundations are solid (see the next axiom “Challenge Assumptions— Especially Your Own”).

它迫使你明确说出你的推理，以验证你的基础是否牢固（见下条公理「挑战假设——尤其是你自己的」）。

It can be used as a starting point to re-evaluate a decision when the condi- • tions that influenced it have changed.

当影响决定的条件变化时，它可以作为重新评估决定的起点。

The effort required to create this documentation is equivalent to jotting down a few notes whenever you have a meeting or discussion on the subject. Whatever the format you choose, this is one type of documentation that is worth the investment.

创建这个文档所需的努力，相当于每次开会或讨论时随手记几个笔记。不管选什么格式，这是一种值得投资的文档。

53. Challenge Assumptions—Especially Your Own

作者：Timothy High

Wethern’s Law of Suspended Judgment states (in a rather tonguein-cheek fashion) that “Assumption is the mother of all screw-ups.” A more popular take on this would be, “Don’t assume—it makes an ‘ass’ of ‘u’ and ‘me’. ” But when you are dealing with assumptions that could cost thousands, if not millions, of dollars it’s not always a laughing matter.

Wethern 悬置判断定律（相当打趣地）说：「假设是所有搞砸之母。」更流行的说法是：「别假设——它让你和我都成了 ass。」但当你处理的假设可能花掉成千甚至上百万美元时，这并不总是好笑的事。

Best practices in software architecture state that you should document the rationale behind each decision that is made, especially when that decision involves a tradeoff (performance versus maintainability, cost versus time-tomarket, and so on). In more formal approaches, it is common to record along with each decision the context of that decision, including the “factors” that contributed to the final judgment. Factors may be functional or nonfunctional requirements, but they also may just be “facts” (or factoids…) that the decision-makers found important (technology constraints, available skill sets, the political environment, etc.).

软件架构最佳实践说你应该记录每个决定背后的理由，特别是当决定涉及权衡时（性能 vs 可维护性、成本 vs 上市时间等）。在更正式的方法里，通常会和每个决定一起记录该决定的上下文，包括促成最终判断的「因素」。因素可以是功能或非功能需求，但也可能只是决策者认为重要的「事实」（或事实碎片……）：技术约束、可用技能集、政治环境等。

This practice is valuable because listing these factors helps highlight assumptions that the architects may have that affect important decisions about the software being designed. Very often these assumptions are based on “historical reasons,” opinion, developer lore, FUDs, or even “something I heard in the hallway”:

这个实践有价值，因为列出这些因素有助于突出架构师可能有的、影响所设计软件重要决定的假设。这些假设经常基于「历史原因」、意见、开发传说、FUD、甚至「我在走廊里听到的什么」：

“Open source is not reliable.” •

「开源不可靠。」

“Bitmap indexes are more trouble than they’re worth.” •

「位图索引得不偿失。」

“The customer would • never accept a page that takes five seconds to load.”

「客户绝不会接受加载要五秒的页面。」

“The CIO would reject anything that isn’t sold by a major vendor.” •

「CIO 会拒绝任何不是大厂商卖的东西。」

It is important to make these assumptions visible and explicit for the sake of posterity and for future re-evaluation. However, it is even more critical to make sure that any assumptions that aren’t based on relevant empirical evidence (or a confirmation from the people involved, for political factors) be validated before a decision is finalized. What if customers can wait five seconds for critical reports if you provide a counter? In exactly what way is exactly which open source project unreliable? Have you tested the bitmap indexes on your data, using your application’s transactions and queries?

为了后世和未来重新评估，让这些假设可见、明确很重要。然而更关键的是，确保任何不基于相关经验证据的假设（或对政治因素相关人员的确认）在决定最终化前被验证。如果提供计数器，客户能等五秒看关键报告吗？到底哪个开源项目到底怎么不可靠？你用你应用的事务和查询在你的数据上测过位图索引吗？

And don’t overlook the word “relevant.” Something that was true in an older version of your software may not be true today. The performance of bitmap indexes in one version of Oracle may not be the same as in another. An older version of a library may have had security holes that have already been fixed. Your old reliable software vendor may be on its last legs financially. The technology landscape changes every day, and so do people. Who knows? Maybe your CIO has become a closet fan of Linux.

别忽略「相关」这个词。在你软件老版本里成立的东西今天可能不成立。一个 Oracle 版本里位图索引的性能可能和另一个版本不同。一个库的老版本可能有已经修复的安全漏洞。你老可靠的软件供应商财务上可能快不行了。技术格局每天都在变，人也在变。谁知道呢？也许你的 CIO 已经成了 Linux 的秘密粉丝。

Facts and assumptions are the pillars on which your software will be built. Whatever they are, make sure the foundations are solid.

事实和假设是你软件将建在其上的支柱。不管它们是什么，确保基础牢固。

54. Share Your Knowledge and Experiences

作者：Paul W. Homer

From all of our experiences , including both success and failure, we learn a great deal. In a young industry like software development, disseminating this experience and knowledge is vital in helping sustain progress. What each team learns in its own tiny little corner of the world is possibly influential across the globe.

从我们所有的经验——包括成功和失败——中学到很多。在软件开发这样年轻的行业里，传播这些经验和知识对维持进步至关重要。每个团队在自己世界小角落里学到的东西，可能影响全球。

Realistically our fundamental knowledge base for software development—that is, the knowledge that is absolute and theoretically correct—is small compared to what is necessary to successfully develop a project. To compensate, we guess, rely on intuitive judgments or even pick randomly. In that, any major development project generates empirical evidence into what works and what fails. We’re gradually working through the permutations, which we want to apply back to the industry as a whole.

现实地说，我们软件开发的基础知识——也就是绝对、理论上正确的知识——和成功开发一个项目所需的相比很小。为了弥补，我们猜、靠直觉判断、甚至随机选。在这过程中，任何大开发项目都产生关于什么有效、什么失败的经验证据。我们在逐渐遍历各种排列组合，想把它应用回整个行业。

At an individual level, we are all trying to grow and come to understand how to build larger and larger systems. The course of our careers will take us toward ever-increasing challenges, for which we want our past experiences to help guide us. Being there is one thing, but to get the most from the experience we often have to rationalize it. The best and easiest way of working through it is to attempt to explain it to another person.

在个人层面，我们都在努力成长，理解怎么建越来越大的系统。我们职业生涯的过程会带我们走向越来越大的挑战，我们希望过去的经验帮我们指引。亲历是一回事，但要从经验中获益最多，我们经常得把它合理化。最好最简单的办法是试图向另一个人解释。

The act of discussing something always helps to show its weaknesses.You don’t really understand something until you can explain it easily. It’s only by putting forth our explanations and discussing them that we solidify the experience into knowledge.

讨论某事的行为总是帮助暴露它的弱点。你不能轻松解释之前，你并没有真正理解。只有提出我们的解释并讨论它们，我们才把经验固化成知识。

Another point is that while we may have had specific experiences, the inferences we draw from them may not be entirely correct in the overall context. We may not have been as successful as we thought, or as smart as we wanted. Of course, testing your knowledge against the real world is scary, particularly when you find out that something dear is myth, incorrect, or was never true; it’s hard to be wrong.

另一点是，虽然我们可能有过具体经验，但我们从中得出的推论在整体上下文中可能不完全正确。我们可能没自己想的那么成功，或没自己希望的那么聪明。当然，用现实世界检验你的知识是吓人的，特别是当你发现珍视的东西是神话、不正确或从来不对；错了很难受。

Ultimately, we are human beings so not everything in our minds is correct; not every thought we have is reasonable. It’s only when we accept our flaws that we open up the possibility of improving. The old adage about learning more from failure always holds. If our ideas and beliefs do not stand the test of a debate, then it is better we find out now than build on it later.

最终，我们是人，所以脑子里不是所有东西都对；不是每个想法都合理。只有接受我们的缺点，我们才打开改进的可能。从失败中学更多的古训总是成立的。如果我们的想法和信念经不起辩论考验，那最好现在发现，而不是以后建在上面。

We really want to share our knowledge and experience to help the industry progress; we also realize it helps us to understand and correct it. Given the state of so much of our software, it is clearly important for us to take every opportunity to share the things we know, what we think we know, and what we’ve seen. If we help those around us to improve, they’ll help us to reach our full potential.

我们真的想分享知识和经验帮行业进步；我们也意识到这帮我们理解和纠正它。鉴于我们软件的现状，清楚的是：我们应该抓住每个机会分享我们知道的、我们以为我们知道的、我们见过的。如果我们帮周围人进步，他们会帮我们发挥全部潜力。

Paul W. Homer Paul W. Homer is a software developer, writer, and occasional photographer, who was drawn into software development several decades ago and has been struggling ever since with trying to build increasingly complex systems.

Paul W. Homer Paul W. Homer 是软件开发者、作家、偶尔摄影师，几十年前被卷入软件开发，此后一直在和试图建越来越复杂系统作斗争。

55. Pattern Pathology

作者：Chad LaVigne

Design patterns are one of the most valuable tools  available to the software architect. Using patterns allows us to create common solutions that are easier to communicate and understand. They are concepts that are directly associated with good design. This fact can make it very enticing to demonstrate our architectural prowess by throwing a lot of patterns at a project. If you find yourself trying to shoehorn your favorite patterns into a problem space where they don’t apply, you may be a victim of pattern pathology.

设计模式是软件架构师可用的最有价值工具之一。用模式让我们创建更容易沟通和理解的共同方案。它们是和好设计直接关联的概念。这个事实让通过在项目上扔一堆模式来展示架构实力非常诱人。如果你发现自己试图把最喜欢的模式硬塞进不适用的问题空间，你可能是模式病理的受害者。

Many projects suffer from this condition. These are the projects where you envision the original architect looking up from the last page in his patterns book, rubbing his hands together and saying, “Now, which one will I use first!?”. This mentality is somewhat akin to that of a developer who begins writing a class with the thought “hmmm, what class should I extend?”. Design patterns are excellent tools for mitigating necessary complexity, but like all tools, they can be misused. Design patterns become a problem when we make them the proverbial hammer with which we must strike every nail. Be careful that your appreciation for patterns doesn’t become an infatuation that has you introducing solutions that are more complicated than they need to be.

很多项目都有这个病。这些就是那种你能想象原架构师从模式书最后一页抬头、搓着手说「现在我先用哪个！？」的项目。这种心态有点像开发开始写类时想「嗯，我该继承哪个类？」。设计模式是缓解必要复杂度的优秀工具，但像所有工具一样，它们会被误用。当我们把它们变成众所周知的锤子、必须敲每个钉子时，设计模式就成了问题。小心你对模式的欣赏不要变成迷恋，让你引入比需要更复杂的方案。

Stamping patterns all over a project unnecessarily is over-engineering. Design patterns are not magic and using them doesn’t automatically qualify a solution as good design. They are reusable solutions to recurring problems. They have been discovered and documented by others to help us recognize when we’re looking at a wheel that’s already been invented. It’s our job to identify problems solved by these solutions when they arise and apply design patterns appropriately. Don’t let your desire to exhibit design pattern knowledge cloud your pragmatic vision. Keep your sights focused on designing systems that provide effective business solutions and use patterns to solve the problems they address.

不必要地在项目上到处盖模式章是过度工程。设计模式不是魔法，用了它们不自动让方案成为好设计。它们是对反复出现问题的可复用方案。它们被别人发现和记录，帮我们认出什么时候看到的是已经发明过的轮子。我们的工作是在这些方案解决的问题出现时识别出来，并适当地应用设计模式。别让你展示设计模式知识的欲望遮蔽你的务实视野。把目光聚焦在设计提供有效业务解决方案的系统上，用模式解决它们处理的问题。

Chad LaVigne Chad LaVigne is a solutions architect and technical hired gun for Baltimore-based TEKSystems, Inc. He works primarily in the Minneapolis area designing and implementing solutions utilizing Enterprise Java technologies.

Chad LaVigne Chad LaVigne 是巴尔的摩 TEKSystems 的解决方案架构师和技术雇用兵。他主要在明尼阿波利斯地区用 Enterprise Java 技术设计和实现方案。

56. Don't Stretch the Architecture Metaphors

作者：David Ing

Architects like to deal with metaphors. They provide nice concrete handles on subjects that are often abstract, complex, and moving targets. Whether it is communicating with the rest of the team or talking through the architecture with the end user, it is so tempting to find something tangible or physical to use as a metaphor for what you are trying to build.

架构师喜欢用隐喻。它们给通常抽象、复杂、移动目标的主题提供具体抓手。不管是和团队其他人沟通还是和终端用户讨论架构，找个有形或物理的东西作你想建之物的隐喻非常诱人。

This usually starts well, in that a common language can evolve where people start to feel that things are moving in the right direction. The metaphor develops and grows over time until it takes on a life of its own. People feel good about the metaphor—we’re making progress!

这通常开头不错，因为共同语言可以演化，人们开始觉得事情在朝对的方向走。隐喻随时间发展成长，直到它有了自己的生命。人们对隐喻感觉良好——我们在进步！

What usually happens is that the metaphor for the architecture now becomes dangerous. Here’s how it can turn on its architect creators:

通常发生的是架构的隐喻变得危险了。它怎么反过来咬它的架构师创造者：

The business domain customer starts to like your metaphor more that • your proposed system, in that the happiest possible interpretation is now shared by all concerned and no real constraints are uncovered.

业务领域客户开始喜欢你的隐喻超过你提的系统，因为最开心的解释现在所有相关方都共享了，没有真正的约束被揭露。

Example: “We’re building a transport system like a ship travelling between a series of docks.”

例子：「我们在建一个运输系统，像一艘船在一系列码头间航行。」

You think container ships crossing the Pacific. I was actually thinking a rowing boat in a swimming pool, with possibly one oar.

你想的是跨太平洋的集装箱船。我其实想的是游泳池里的划艇，可能还有一个桨。

The development team starts to think that the metaphor is more impor- • tant than the actual business problem. You start to justify odd decisions because of a fondness for the metaphor.

开发团队开始觉得隐喻比实际业务问题更重要。你因为喜欢隐喻开始为奇怪的决定辩护。

Example: “We said it’s like a filing cabinet, so of course we have to show it to the user alphabetically. I know it’s a filing cabinet with six dimensions and of infinite length and with a clock built in to it, but we’ve done the icon now—so it has to be a filing cabinet…”.

例子：「我们说过它像文件柜，所以当然必须按字母顺序展示给用户。我知道这是个六维、无限长、还内建时钟的文件柜，但图标已经画好了——所以它必须是文件柜……」

The delivered system contains relics of names from old, broken metaphors • long gone—archaeological testimonials to concepts long refactored and dug over.

交付的系统包含早已破碎的旧隐喻名字遗迹——考古学上对早已被重构和翻掘的概念的证明。

Example: “Why does the Billing Factory object create a Port channel for the Rowing boat system? Surely it should return a Pomegranate view for the Hub Bus? What do you mean you’re new here?”

例子：「为什么 Billing Factory 对象给划艇系统创建一个 Port 通道？它难道不该为 Hub Bus 返回一个 Pomegranate 视图？你说你新来的是什么意思？」

So remember, don’t fall in love with your system metaphor—only use it for exploratory communication purposes, and don’t let it turn on you.

所以记住，别爱上你的系统隐喻——只用它做探索性沟通，别让它反过来咬你。

David Ing David Ing is a software architect/technologist living and working in Vancouver, British Columbia. Originally from the U.K., he moved across to get away from the rain, although now feels tricked by dishonest tourist literature. As fashion dictates, he now works at Web 2.0 company Taglocity, where he splits his time trying to make email systems “less awful” and figure out what Web 2.0 actually means.

David Ing David Ing 是住在温哥华的软件架构师/技术专家。英国人，搬过来是为了躲雨，虽然现在觉得被不实旅游文学骗了。他现在在 Web 2.0 公司 Taglocity 工作，一半时间在让邮件系统「不那么糟」，一半时间在搞清楚 Web 2.0 到底是什么意思。

57. Focus on Application Support and Maintenance

作者：Mncedisi Kasper

The support and maintenance of an application should never, ever be an afterthought. Since over 80% of an application’s lifecycle is spent in maintenance, you should pay a lot of attention to the problems of support and maintenance when you’re designing. Fail to heed this, and you’ll watch with horror as your application stops being the architect’s dream and becomes a vile beast that dies a horrible death and is forever remembered as a failure.

应用的支持和维护永远永远不该是事后想法。因为应用生命周期 80% 以上在维护中度过，你设计时应该非常关注支持和维护问题。不听这个，你会惊恐地看着你的应用不再是架构师的梦，而是变成一只死掉惨不忍睹、永远被记住为失败的邪恶魔兽。

When most architects design applications, they think mainly of developers, who have IDEs and debuggers in place. If something goes wrong, highly skilled software engineers debug away and the bug is discovered. It’s easy to think this way because most architects have spent most of their lives as developers rather than administrators. Unfortunately, the developer and the support guy have different skill sets, just as the development/testing environment and the production environment have different purposes.

大多数架构师设计应用时主要想开发——他们有 IDE 和调试器。出问题时，高技能软件工程师调试一下，bug 就找到了。这么想很容易，因为大多数架构师一辈子大部分时间是开发而不是管理员。不幸的是，开发和支持人员技能集不同，就像开发/测试环境和生产环境用途不同。

Here are a few of the disadvantages that an administrator faces:

管理员面对的几个劣势：

An administrator can’t resubmit a request message to reproduce the prob- • lem. When you’re in production, you can’t reissue a financial transaction against the “live” database to see what went wrong.

管理员不能重发请求消息重现问题。在生产环境，你不能对「活」数据库重发金融交易看出了什么问题。

Once the application is in production, the pressure to fix bugs comes from • customers and executives, not from the project manager and the testing team—and an angry CEO can be a lot more threatening.

应用一上生产，修 bug 的压力来自客户和高管，不是项目经理和测试团队——愤怒的 CEO 有威胁多了。

Once you’re in production, there is no debugger. •

一上生产，没有调试器。

Once you’re in production, deployment needs to be scheduled and co- • ordinated. You can’t take a production application down for a few minutes to test a bug fix.

一上生产，部署需要调度和协调。你不能把生产应用停几分钟测一个 bug 修复。

The logging level is much higher in the development environment than • in production.

开发环境日志级别比生产高得多。

A few symptoms of this failure to plan for support are:

这种不为支持做计划的几个症状：

Most problems require a developer’s involvement. •

大多数问题需要开发介入。

The relationship between the development team and the support team is • sour; the developers think the support team is a bunch of idiots.

开发团队和支持团队关系变酸；开发觉得支持团队是一群白痴。

The support team hates the new application. •

支持团队恨新应用。

The architect and development teams are spending a lot of time in • ­production.

架构师和开发团队在生产里花很多时间。

The application is restarted often as a way to resolve problems. •

应用经常被重启作为解决问题的方式。

The administrators never have time to tune the system properly because • they’re always fighting fires.

管理员永远没时间好好调优系统，因为他们一直在救火。

To ensure that your application succeeds once it’s out of the developers’ hands, you should:

为确保你的应用一离开开发之手就成功，你应该：

Understand that development and support require a different skill set. •

理解开发和支持需要不同技能集。

Get a support lead as early in on the project as possible. •

项目尽早拉一个支持负责人进来。

Make the support lead a core part of the team. •

让支持负责人成为团队核心。

Involve a support lead with the planning for the application support. •

让支持负责人参与应用支持规划。

Design such that the learning curve for the support personnel is minimal. Traceability, auditing, and logging are crucial. When the administrators are happy, everybody is happy (especially your boss).

设计时让支持人员学习曲线最小。可追溯性、审计和日志至关重要。管理员开心了，大家都开心（特别是你老板）。

Mncedisi Kasper Mncedisi Kasper is a director of technology and strategy at Open Xcellence ICT Solutions, a South Africa–based company specializing in enterprise application integration and SAP (ABAP/XI) consultancy.

Mncedisi Kasper Mncedisi Kasper 是 Open Xcellence ICT Solutions 的技术和战略总监，这是一家南非公司，专责企业应用集成和 SAP（ABAP/XI）咨询。

58. Prepare to Pick Two

作者：Bill de hÓra

Sometimes accepting a constraint  or giving up on a property can lead to a better architecture, one that is easier and less expensive to build and run. Like buses, desirable properties tend to come in threes, and trying to define and build a system that supports all three can result in a system that does nothing especially well.

有时候接受一个约束或放弃一个属性会带来更好的架构——一个更容易、更便宜构建和运行的架构。像公交车一样，想要的属性往往三个一来，试图定义和构建一个支持所有三个的系统，结果可能是什么都做不好的系统。

A famous example is Brewer’s conjecture, also known as Consistency, Availability, and Partitioning (CAP), which states that there are three properties that are commonly desired in a distributed system—consistency, availability, and partition tolerance—and that it is impossible to achieve all three. Trying to have all three will drastically increase the engineering costs and typically increase complexity without actually achieving the desired effect or business goal. If your data must be available and distributed, achieving consistency becomes increasingly expensive and eventually impossible. Likewise, if the system must be distributed and consistent, ensuring consistency will lead at first to latency and performance problems and eventually to unavailability since the system cannot be exposed as it tries to reaches agreement.

一个著名例子是 Brewer 猜想，也就是一致性、可用性、分区容错（CAP）定理，说分布式系统有三个通常想要的属性——一致性、可用性、分区容错——不可能全部达到。试图全要会大幅增加工程成本，通常增加复杂度却不真正达到期望效果或业务目标。如果你的数据必须可用和分布式，达成一致性变得越来越贵、最终不可能。同样，如果系统必须分布式和一致，确保一致性首先导致延迟和性能问题，最终导致不可用——因为系统试图达成协议时不能被暴露。

It’s often the case that one or more properties are considered inviolate: data cannot be duplicated, all writes must be transactional, the system must be

经常一个或多个属性被认为不可侵犯：数据不能复制、所有写必须事务、系统必须

100% available, calls must be asynchronous, there must be no single point of failure, everything must be extensible, and so on. Apart from being naïve, treating properties as religious artifacts will stop you from thinking about the problem at hand. We start to talk about architectural deviation instead of principled design and we confuse dogmatism with good governance. Instead we should ask, why must these properties hold? What benefit is to be had by doing so? When are these properties desirable? How can we break up the system to achieve a better result? Be ever the skeptic, because architectural dogma tends to undermine delivery. The inevitability of such tradeoffs is one of the most difficult things to accept in software development, not just as architects, but also as developers and stakeholders. But we should cherish them; it’s far better than having limitless choice, and accepting tradeoffs often induces a creative and inventive result.

100% 可用、调用必须异步、不能有单点故障、一切必须可扩展等等。除了天真之外，把属性当宗教圣物会阻止你思考眼前的问题。我们开始谈架构偏离而不是有原则的设计，把教条和好治理混为一谈。相反我们应该问：为什么这些属性必须成立？这么做有什么好处？这些属性什么时候是想要的？我们怎么拆系统得到更好结果？永远做怀疑者，因为架构教条倾向于破坏交付。这种权衡的必然性是软件开发中最难接受的事之一——不仅对架构师，对开发和干系人也是。但我们应该珍惜它们；这比无限选择好得多，接受权衡经常带来创造性和发明性的结果。

Bill de hÓra Bill de hÓra is chief architect with NewBay Software, where he works on large scale web and mobile systems. He is co-editor of the Atom Publishing Protocol and previously served on the W3C RDF Working Group. He is a recognized expert on REST style and message-passing architectures and protocol design.

Bill de hÓra Bill de hÓra 是 NewBay Software 的首席架构师，做大规模 Web 和移动系统。他是 Atom Publishing Protocol 的共同编辑，之前在 W3C RDF 工作组。他是 REST 风格和消息传递架构与协议设计的公认专家。

59. Prefer Principles, Axioms, and Analogies to Opinion and Taste

作者：Michael Harmer

When creating your architecture  you should explicitly use principles, axioms, and analogies to guide the creation. This gives the architecture a number of benefits that are not present if you simply create by implicitly leveraging your experience, opinions, and tastes.

创建架构时，你应该明确用原则、公理和类比来指导创建。这给架构带来几个好处——如果你只是隐式利用你的经验、意见和品味来创建，这些好处就没有。

Documenting your architecture will be easier. You can start by describing the principles that were followed. This is much easier than trying to communicate your opinions and experience. The principles will then provide a convenient handle for those tasked with understanding and implementing the architecture. It will also be invaluable for subsequent or inexperienced architects who need to work with the architecture.

记录架构会更容易。你可以从描述遵循的原则开始。这比试图传达你的意见和经验容易得多。这些原则然后给那些要理解和实现架构的人一个方便抓手。对后续或没经验的架构师也极有价值。

An architecture with clear principles is an architecture that frees its architect from reviewing everything and being everywhere. It gives architects greater leverage and influence. You will not need to be an omniscient workaholic to ensure that others can consistently:

有清晰原则的架构是把架构师从什么都要审、到处都在的状态解放出来的架构。它给架构师更大的杠杆和影响。你不需要成为全知工作狂就能确保别人能一致地：

Implement and adapt the architecture •

实现和适配架构

Extend the architecture into related domains •

把架构扩展到相关领域

Reimplement the architecture using newer technologies •

用更新技术重实现架构

Work out the detailed edge cases •

搞清楚详细边界情况

Disagreements about opinion and taste invariably turn into political arguments in which authority is used to win. However, disagreements where the foundation principles are clear provide a way for more reasoned discussion to occur without issues being personalised. It also allows the disagreements to be resolved without reference to the architect at all.

关于意见和品味的分歧总会变成用权威取胜的政治争论。然而，基础原则清晰的分歧提供了更理性讨论的方式，问题不被个人化。它还允许分歧完全不参考架构师就解决。

Principles and axioms also give an architecture consistency throughout its implementation and across time. Consistency is often a problem, especially in large systems that span multiple technologies and will exist for many years. Clear architectural principles allow those unfamiliar with a particular technology or component to reason about and more readily understand the unfamiliar technology.

原则和公理还给架构跨实现和跨时间的一致性。一致性经常是问题，特别是跨多技术、存在多年的大系统。清晰的架构原则让不熟悉某技术或组件的人能推理和更容易理解不熟悉的技术。

Michael Harmer Michael Harmer has worked in software for 16 years as a developer, team leader, architect, principal engineer, and practice manager.

Michael Harmer Michael Harmer 在软件业工作 16 年，做过开发、团队负责人、架构师、首席工程师和实践经理。

60. Start with a Walking Skeleton

作者：Clint Shank

One very useful strategy for implementing, verifying, and evolving an application architecture is to start with what Alistair Cockburn calls a walking skeleton . A walking skeleton is a minimal, end-to-end implementation of the system that links together all the main architectural components. Starting small, with a working system exercising all the communication paths, gives you confidence that you are heading in the right direction.

实现、验证和演化应用架构一个非常有用的策略是从 Alistair Cockburn 所谓的「行走骨架」开始。行走骨架是系统最小的端到端实现，把所有主要架构组件连起来。从小开始，用一个跑通所有通信路径的工作系统，让你有信心走在对的方向上。

Once the skeleton is in place, it’s time to put it on a workout program. Bulk it up with full body workouts. This means implement incrementally, adding end-to-end functionality. The goal is to keep the system running, all the while growing the skeleton.

骨架到位后，是时候上锻炼计划了。用全身锻炼让它长肉。这意味着增量实现，加端到端功能。目标是保持系统跑着，同时一直长骨架。

Making changes to an architecture is harder and more expensive the longer it has been around and the bigger it gets. We want to find mistakes early. This approach gives us a short feedback cycle from which we can more quickly adapt and work iteratively as necessary to meet the business’s prioritized list of runtime-discernable quality attributes. Assumptions about the architecture are validated earlier. The architecture is more easily evolved because problems are found at an earlier stage when less has been invested in its implementation.

对架构做改动越久、越大就越难越贵。我们想早发现错误。这个方法给我们短反馈循环，让我们能更快适应、按需迭代以满足业务排了优先级的运行时可辨别质量属性列表。关于架构的假设更早被验证。架构更容易演化，因为问题在早期阶段被发现——那时实现投入还少。

The bigger the system, the more important it is to use this strategy. In a small application, one developer can implement a feature from top to bottom relatively quickly, but this becomes impractical with larger systems. It is quite common to have multiple developers on a single team or even on multiple, possibly distributed, teams involved in implementing end-to-end. Consequently, more coordination is necessary. And naturally, developers implement at a different pace. Some developers can accomplish a lot and in little time while others can spend a lot of time implementing very little. More difficult and time consuming efforts should be done earlier in the project.

系统越大，用这个策略越重要。在小应用里，一个开发可以相对快地端到端实现一个功能，但这在大系统里不现实。单个团队甚至多个可能分布式团队的多个开发参与端到端实现很常见。因此需要更多协调。自然，开发实现速度不同。有些开发短时间能做很多，另一些花很多时间做很少。更难更耗时的努力应该在项目早期做。

Clint Shank Clint Shank is a software developer, consultant, and mentor at Sphere of Influence, Inc., a software design and engineering services company for commercial and federal clients.

Clint Shank Clint Shank 是 Sphere of Influence, Inc.（为商业和联邦客户提供软件设计和工程服务的公司）的软件开发、顾问和导师。
